thread.title: Here's how Apple plans to overcome lower Q1 revenue projections (AAPL)

author: Rayna Hollander
title: Here's how Apple plans to overcome lower Q1 revenue projections (AAPL)
text: Rayna Hollander 6m This story was delivered to Business Insider Intelligence Apps and Platforms Briefing subscribers hours before appearing on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here . Apple issued a surprise warning on its fiscal Q1 2019 (ended December 29, 2018) revenue guidance in a letter to investors on Wednesday. This marks the first time in 16 years that Apple reduced revenue expectations; the company lowered its expected range of $89 billion-$93 billion in revenue to $84 billion, which is a 5% decline from the same quarter last year. Business Insider Intelligence Apple attributed the weakened revenue projection to a variety of factors, including lower than expected iPhone upgrades, particularly in Greater China, and a waning economy in Greater China. Apple CEO Tim Cook credited the slowdown in upgrades to the shift away from carrier subsidies, price increases based on the strength of the US dollar, and cheaper iPhone battery replacements. Nevertheless, Apple highlighted a few steps it will take to resolve its iPhone upgrade problem and reverse the revenue downturn in the quarters ahead. Ramping up advertisements of its trade-in program. Apple plans to lean more on its trade-in program , which was first introduced in 2015, to better offset the climbing iPhone selling prices, especially since fewer carriers are offering subsidies of new phones. With the program, a customer who trades in their iPhone 7 Plus can purchase an iPhone XR, which retails for $749, for $449, or an iPhone XS, which retails for $999, for $699. Better incentivizing upgrades with trade-in rebates can help convince more consumers to make the switch. Enhancing customer support for iPhone upgrades. Consumers are often highly concerned about data transfers when switching to new devices, according to Cook. By increasing its focus on in-store customer service, Apple plans to alleviate consumers' apprehension about losing data when upgrading, which could increase consumer willingness to purchase a new device. Introducing payment installment plans for new iPhones. While most major US wireless carriers enable consumers to pay in monthly installments, Apple plans to expand the program. However, details on how Apple plans to do so aren't available yet. The news means Apple's facing more pressure than ever to deliver on another successful product that can diversify its revenue beyond the iPhone. The iPhone is the most important player in Apple's current strategy, because it's the cynosure of a consumer's connected ecosystem. The iPhone segment accounted for 59% of Apple's overall revenue in its fiscal Q4 2018. And the more iPhone users there are, the more chances Apple will have to sell to consumers who want to expand their selection of products to smartwatches, smart speakers, and headphones, since most likely prefer to stay within the same ecosystem. But as iPhone sales flatten, Apple should consider shifting focus toward products such as AR smart glasses and the connected car, which can help the company break free from its overreliance on iPhone sales and one day displace the smartphone.
